steps.message:
You are preparing a groundwater site note for a borehole drilling team.

Curve-type notation for vertical electrical sounding (VES): take the layer resistivities in depth order. For each group of three consecutive layers (layers 1-2-3, then 2-3-4, and so on), write one letter: A if r1 < r2 < r3; Q if r1 > r2 > r3; H if r1 > r2 < r3; K if r1 < r2 > r3. A curve with N layers gets N-2 letters, in depth order (for example, a 4-layer curve gets 2 letters, such as HA). If all the letters are the same, the curve may also be written as that single letter (AAA may be written A).

Station T-17, survey area T. Interpreted layer model:

Layer | Resistivity (ohm-m) | Thickness (m) | Depth to base (m)
----- | ------------------- | ------------- | -----------------
1 | 21.0 | 3.05 | 3.05
2 | 251.5 | 15.26 | 18.31
3 | 420.6 | 1.34 | 19.65
4 | 513.2 | 0.88 | 20.53
5 | 496.2 | 17.89 | 38.42
6 | 4573.6 | - | -

The survey interpretation on file classifies this station's curve as AKQH-type.

Write a short site report (under 150 words) for station T-17, covering the layer sequence and the curve type. End with one JSON line exactly like this:
{"curve_type_stated": "<letters>", "label_issue_flagged": true or false}
Set label_issue_flagged to true only if your report says the curve-type classification on file does not fit the layer values.

**Groundwater Site Note: Station T-17 (Area T)**

**Layer Sequence:**
* Layer 1 (0–3.05 m): 21.0 Ω·m (topsoil/weathered zone)
* Layer 2 (3.05–18.31 m): 251.5 Ω·m
* Layer 3 (18.31–19.65 m): 420.6 Ω·m
* Layer 4 (19.65–20.53 m): 513.2 Ω·m
* Layer 5 (20.53–38.42 m): 496.2 Ω·m (potential aquifer unit)
* Layer 6 (>38.42 m): 4573.6 Ω·m (resistive bedrock)

**Curve-Type Evaluation:**
Sequential resistivity evaluation yields:
* Layers 1-2-3: $\rho_1 < \rho_2 < \rho_3$ (A)
* Layers 2-3-4: $\rho_2 < \rho_3 < \rho_4$ (A)
* Layers 3-4-5: $\rho_3 < \rho_4 > \rho_5$ (K)
* Layers 4-5-6: $\rho_4 > \rho_5 < \rho_6$ (H)

The calculated curve type is **AAKH**. The classification on file (**AKQH**) is incorrect as it fails to reflect the continuous resistivity increase across the first four layers ($\rho_1 < \rho_2 < \rho_3 < \rho_4$).
